deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The bundle is Riemann's 1855 work on Abelian functions. The neighbouring pages count branch points and moduli, and introduce the normalised integrals u_ι with periods πi·δ and a_{ι,ι'} and the theta exponent Σ m_ι m_ι' a_{ι,ι'} + 2 Σ u_ι m_ι. On this page Riemann runs his period-relation (boundary integral) argument one level higher. He applies it to 'second-order' integrals w_{ι',ι''} = ∫ u_ι' du_ι'', which are not Abelian integrals with constant periods. They are what are now called length-2 iterated integrals.

NOTATION (my interpretation, consistent throughout the page).
- Unnormalised basis: a_{ι,ι'} and b_{ι,ι'} are the moduli of periodicity of u_ι' across the two cuts of the ι-th pair in the canonical dissection F** of the surface.
- a_{ι,ι',ι''} and b_{ι,ι',ι''} are the corresponding constants for w_{ι',ι''}. Across a cut, u_ι' jumps by a constant A, so w_{ι',ι''} jumps by A·u_ι'' + const. The 'triple' periods are these constants, defined via the values w^{ι,1}, w^{ι,2}, w^{ι,3} on the banks of the cuts. This is why the page has lines like a_{ι''',ι',ι''} = w^{ι''',3}_{ι',ι''} − w^{ι''',1}_{ι',ι''} + ... and a_{ι''',ι} = w^{ι''',3}_ι − w^{ι''',1}_ι.

(1) Main relation. Riemann defines Σ_ι = ∫ w_{ι',ι''} du_ι''' taken over the whole boundary of F** in the positive sense. The integrand w du''' has d(w du''') = u' du''∧du''' = 0 for holomorphic differentials, so the boundary integral vanishes. Evaluating it pair by pair:
- Opposite banks differ by period constants and by period × u.
- Each cut pair ι therefore contributes the expression in the first two lines: −b_{ι,ι'} a_{ι,ι'',ι'''} + b_{ι,ι'''} a_{ι,ι',ι''} + b_{ι,ι'''}(a_{ι,ι'}a_{ι,ι''} + 2a_{ι,ι''}b_{ι,ι'} − b_{ι,ι''}a_{ι,ι'}) + a_{ι,ι'} b_{ι,ι'',ι'''} − a_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι,ι',ι''} + a_{ι,ι'''}(b_{ι,ι'}b_{ι,ι''} + 2b_{ι,ι''}a_{ι,ι'} − a_{ι,ι''}b_{ι,ι'}).
- Summed over ι this equals 0. The result is a relation that is bilinear in (ordinary period) × (second-order period) plus cubic in ordinary periods. It holds for every triple ι', ι'', ι'''.

(2) The line 0 = Σ(a_{ι,ι'} b_{ι,ι'',ι'''} − a_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι,ι',ι''}) ± ... restates this, with case distinctions ι' ≷ ι'', ι'' ≷ ι''' attached. The quadratic terms depend on the order of the indices, i.e. on the order of the cuts, because second-order periods depend on base point and path.

(3) Normalisation. He substitutes a_{ι,ι'} = πi δ_{ι,ι'}; the old b_{ι,ι'} become the normalised moduli, written a again. The relation collapses to:
−πi a_{ι',ι'',ι'''} + πi a_{ι''',ι',ι''} + πi a_{ι''',ι'}a_{ι''',ι''} − 2πi a_{ι'',ι'''}a_{ι'',ι'} + πi a_{ι',ι'''}a_{ι',ι''} + 2πi b_{ι,ι'''}a_{ι''',ι''} − πi b_{ι'',ι'''}a_{ι'',ι'} − πi b_{ι,ι''}a_{ι',ι'''} (+ Σ terms).
The boxed terms are the remaining contributions. He then isolates the combinations a_{ι',ι'',ι'''} − a_{ι''',ι',ι''} and a_{ι''',ι',ι''} − a_{ι'',ι''',ι'}, the cyclic differences that the relation controls.

(4) Renormalising w. He forms w_{ι',ι''} − Σ_ι u_ι b_{ι,ι',ι''} − u_ι'' πi a_{ι'',ι'} + u_ι' πi a_{ι',ι'}(?). This subtracts linear combinations of the u's from w to kill part of its periods. It is the analogue of normalising an Abelian integral, and is legitimate because w is only defined up to adding c·u + const. He then rewrites the relation for the modified function: πi a_{ι''',ι',ι''} + Σ_ι a_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι,ι',ι''} − πi a_{ι'',ι'}(a_{ι'',ι'''} − a_{ι',ι'''}) + πi a_{ι''',ι''} b_{ι',ι'''} − πi a_{ι''',ι'} b_{ι'',ι'''}.

(5) Jump of w across the ι-th cut. The combination Σ_ι(b_{ι,ι',ι''} + b_{ι,ι'}a_{ι,ι''} − b_{ι,ι''}a_{ι,ι'}) u_ι appears. He then writes:
w^{ι2}_{ι',ι''} − w^{ι1}_{ι',ι''} = b_{ι,ι'}(2u^{ι1}_{ι''}(?) + b_{ι,ι''}) − b_{ι,ι'}a_{ι,ι''} + b_{ι,ι''}a_{ι,ι'} + b_{ι,ι',ι''} + (1/πi) Σ_{ι'''} b_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι''',ι',ι''}.
This is the general form 'period × u on one bank + constant'. Below a rule, the corrected constant is written as c_{ι,ι',ι''} − (1/πi) Σ_{ι'''} a_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι''',ι',ι''}. This is the change of the second-order period constants under the renormalisation in (4).

PURPOSE. Riemann is working out the multiplicative or 'quadratic' periodicity of the integrals ∫u du and the transcendental relations their periods must satisfy. This plausibly connects to the next page's question of how many transcendental relations exist among the a_{ι,ι'}.
errors: The page is a scratch computation. Several index slips are likely: e.g. 'u_ι' πi a_{ι',ι'}' (probably a_{ι'',ι'} or similar), 'a_{ι'',ι''}' in the line '+a_{ι'',ι''} πi b_{ι',ι'''}' (likely a_{ι''',ι''}), and the '2' in 'b_{ι,ι'}(2u...)'. These cannot be confirmed without fixing his conventions.

The second-order periods depend on base point, on the order of the cuts, and on how w is continued across the dissection. The page does not state these conventions explicitly; they are encoded only in the bank superscripts w^{ι,1}, w^{ι,2}, w^{ι,3}. Signs of the quadratic terms (e.g. the factor 2 in 2a_{ι,ι''}b_{ι,ι'}) are plausible but not independently verifiable from the page alone.

The mixture of 'b_{ι,ι'''}' with the normalised a's in the line after normalisation (2 b_{ι,ι'''} πi a_{ι''',ι''}) suggests the substitution was only partially carried out. The free index ι should have been summed or eliminated.

results.what: Vanishing of the boundary integral ∫_{∂F**} w_{ι',ι''} du_ι''' (w = ∫u_ι' du_ι''), evaluated cut by cut. This gives a relation among ordinary periods and periods of second-order (iterated) integrals, bilinear in mixed form plus cubic in ordinary periods.
results.modern_name: Period relations for length-2/length-3 iterated integrals on a compact Riemann surface (higher analogue of Riemann's bilinear relations; Chen iterated integrals, 'quadratic periods')
results.usually_credited_to: K.-T. Chen (iterated integrals, 1970s); R. C. Gunning ('quadratic periods' of Abelian integrals, 1970s); R. Hain, B. Harris (1980s, mixed Hodge structure on π1, harmonic volume)

results.what: Jump of w_{ι',ι''} across a cut equals (period of u_ι') × u_ι'' + constant. Renormalisation of w by subtracting linear combinations of the u_ι, with the corresponding transformation of the second-order period constants.
results.modern_name: Multiplicative/unipotent monodromy of iterated integrals; change of basepoint/normalisation for quadratic periods
results.usually_credited_to: Chen, Gunning (20th century); implicit in Poincaré's work on iterated monodromy

results.what: Normalisation a_{ι,ι'} = πi δ_{ι,ι'} applied to the relation.

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's bilinear relations and the dissection method are well known as his. What is non-standard is extending the boundary-integral argument to ∫(∫u du)du, i.e. deriving relations among periods of iterated integrals. That topic is usually associated with Chen, Gunning, Hain and Harris a century later. The page is fragmentary and its conventions are implicit, so its correctness cannot be fully confirmed. I am also unaware of literature crediting Riemann with it. Hence a notable but not major surprise.

checkable.sympy: x,A=symbols('x A'); u1=Function('u1')(x); u2=Function('u2')(x); w=Function('w')(x); expr = diff(w + A*u2, x) - (u1 + A)*diff(u2, x); simplify(expr.subs(diff(w,x), u1*diff(u2,x))) == 0
checkable.asserts: If dw = u1 du2 and u1 jumps by the constant A, then w jumps by A*u2 + const. This is the form of the jump formula w^{ι2} − w^{ι1} on the page.

checkable.sympy: t,s=symbols('t s'); f1=1+2*t; f2=3*t**2; I1=integrate(f1,(t,0,1)); I2=integrate(f2,(t,0,1)); I12=integrate(f1.subs(t,s)*integrate(f2,(t,0,s)).subs(s,s),(s,0,1)); I21=integrate(f2.subs(t,s)*integrate(f1,(t,0,s)),(s,0,1)); simplify(I12+I21-I1*I2)==0
checkable.asserts: Shuffle relation for length-2 iterated integrals: ∫ω1ω2 + ∫ω2ω1 = ∫ω1·∫ω2. Equivalently w_{ι',ι''} + w_{ι'',ι'} = u_ι' u_ι'' + const, which links a_{ι,ι',ι''} and a_{ι,ι'',ι'}.

checkable.sympy: X1,X2,X3=symbols('X1 X2 X3',commutative=False); A=symbols('A1:4'); B=symbols('B1:4'); a=sum(A[i]*[X1,X2,X3][i] for i in range(3)); b=sum(B[i]*[X1,X2,X3][i] for i in range(3)); # truncated exp: E(x)=1+x+x**2/2+x**3/6; C=E(a)*E(b)*E(-a)*E(-b) expanded to degree 3; coefficient of X1*X2 minus X2*X1 equals A1*B2-A2*B1
checkable.asserts: Chen/BCH model of one cut pair, with exponents restricted to their degree-1 parts: the degree-2 part of the commutator loop gives the ordinary bilinear term A1*B2 − B1*A2 (Riemann's period relation).

checkable.sympy: # same setup with a=a1+a2, b=b1+b2 where a2,b2 are general degree-2 Lie elements built from second-order periods; log(e^a e^b e^-a e^-b) degree-3 part = [a1,b2]+[a2,b1]+(1/2)[a1,[a1,b1]]+(1/2)[b1,[a1,b1]]; summing over cut pairs and setting coefficients of X_j*X_k*X_l to zero
checkable.asserts: Gives the cubic relation among first- and second-order periods (vanishing of the length-3 iterated integral around ∂F**). A CAS can compare its X_ι'X_ι''X_ι''' coefficient with Riemann's per-cut expression −b a_{ι'' ι'''} + b a_{ι' ι''} + b(aa + 2ab − ba) + ..., after fixing sign conventions.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the phrase after F** is probably 'in positivem Sinne genommen' (or 'in positiver Richtung genommen'). 'Dimension' is unlikely; compare the next page's 'in positivem Sinne durchlaufen'.

In 'b_{ι,ι'}(ι1/(2u_{ι''}) + b_{ι,ι''})' the fraction is almost certainly a misreading of a stacked superscript: read 2u^{ι1}_{ι''} (the value of u_ι'' on bank 1 of cut ι), giving b_{ι,ι'}(2u^{ι1}_{ι''} + b_{ι,ι''}).

In the line 'w_{ι',ι''} − Σu_ι b_{ι,ι',ι''} − u_{ι''}πi a_{ι'',ι'} + u_{ι'} πi a_{ι',ι'}' the last factor is likely a_{ι'',ι'} or a_{ι',ι''}, not a_{ι',ι'}. Also check whether 'w_{ι'}' is meant instead of 'u_{ι'}'.
'+ a_{ι'',ι''} πi · b_{ι',ι'''}' likely reads a_{ι''',ι''} in the image.
The bracketed '[-a-]' in the line '+ (1/πi) Σ_{ι'''} [-a-] b_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι''',ι',ι''}' is a struck-through letter. The surviving symbol is b, but in the parallel line below it is a_{ι,ι'''}.
The superscripts on w (w^{ι''',3}, w^{ι''',1}, w^{ι2}, w^{ι1}) are bank labels of the cuts, not powers.
